topic_development_chronological.development: This reopened the sharing question concretely. topic_development_chronological.topic: User pushed back: don't want to re-run this manually every time
topic_development_chronological.development: User asked whether it would be easier to just permanently write relative paths going forward, given how much iterative work remains ahead. This shifted the solution from 'one-time export step' to 'permanent architectural fix.' A shared helper module was proposed: scripts/paths.py, defining PROJECT_ROOT anchored to the helper file's own location (Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent) rather than the current working directory — explicitly chosen for robustness against being invoked from different working directories (VS Code run button vs terminal vs a teammate's differently-nested copy). Two functions: to_relative() for writing, resolve_path() for reading. The user was walked through exactly which existing scripts needed to import to_relative() (every script that writes a path into a CSV: organize_asvspoof.py, chunk_deep_voice.py, resample_gary_stafford_real.py, build_metadata.py) versus resolve_path() (every script that reads a path back out to open a file: audit_datasets.py, validate_metadata.py, check_actual_channels.py, and the future extract_features.py).

topic_development_chronological.topic: User asked whether deferring the retrofit and 'handling it when it comes up' was acceptable
topic_development_chronological.development: Answered honestly: deferring would not cause a crash later (Python's pathlib handles absolute paths gracefully even when a relative-path resolver is applied to them), so nothing would break for the user personally — but it would fail silently the next time a zip was shared with teammates, since master_metadata.csv would quietly contain absolute paths again with no error or warning. This reframed the choice as a discipline tradeoff (retrofit once now vs. remember to always re-run a conversion script before every future share) rather than a correctness question, and confirmed that running the one-time conversion before the immediate/current zip was non-negotiable regardless of which path forward was chosen.

topic_development_chronological.development: User applied the requested fix correctly (verified: both parent_file: to_relative(filepath) instances present and correct). Running the script threw ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'librosa'.
